articleTitle: High-order current-mode continuous-time multiple output OTA capacitor filters
publicationTitle: IEE 15th SARAGA Colloquium on Digital and Analogue Filters and Filtering Systems
abstract: A systematic method is presented for generation and design of current-mode continuous-time multiple integrator loop all-pole filters using dual output operational transconductance amplifiers and capacitors (DO-OTA-C). A number of architectures including canonical realizations are developed, with particular emphasis on high-order configurations. These current-mode DO-OTA-C filter structures have various interesting advantages.

articleTitle: The design of analogue and digital filters using genetic algorithms
publicationTitle: IEE 15th SARAGA Colloquium on Digital and Analogue Filters and Filtering Systems
abstract: The conventional approach to filter design is to select one of the standard polynomial transfer functions that satisfies the response specification, followed by the implementation of the transfer function in one of the standard circuit structures. In many cases this approach is inadequate and an optimisation approach is required. The need for this can arise in a various ways, including non-standard response specification, and the consideration of practical effects such as finite-arithmetic effects and computational complexity for digital filters, and component selection and device imperfections in analogue filters. Classical hill-climbing optimisation methods have succeeded in certain cases but are less suited to the general design task which can be mixed discrete/continuous, can have many local minima, and have high dimensionality. Recently genetic algorithm (GA) optimisation methods have emerged as a powerful approach to solving the more difficult optimisation problems. Publications are emerging in the literature on GAs applied to filter design and promise to move filter design significantly forwards to the ultimate goal of a single-step design from general specification to full practical implementation. This paper aims to: give a brief tutorial on GAs; provide a set of commented references on GAs applied to filter design; and present some new work on single-step design of finite wordlength (FWL) IIR digital filters that simultaneously satisfy magnitude and phase template specifications.

articleTitle: Ideas and concepts for the automation of analogue filters using qualitative reasoning
publicationTitle: IEE 15th SARAGA Colloquium on Digital and Analogue Filters and Filtering Systems
abstract: We have presented some ideas for the automated design of analogue integrated systems using qualitative reasoning and design automation concepts. The prototype system with a qualitative system optimiser is currently being implemented in C and turbo Prolog on an IBM PC compatible. At the moment only simple SC filter examples are considered but we hope to extend the approach to ADCc and PLLs. Qualitative algorithms should be seriously considered in view of the much increased complexity of the analogue design process and the consequent need for systematic and well-reasoned assistance and simplification.

articleTitle: Improved IIR adaptive line enhancement for tracking sinusoids in noise
publicationTitle: IEE 15th SARAGA Colloquium on Digital and Analogue Filters and Filtering Systems
abstract: The classical problem of extracting an unknown sinusoid from a noise background has many partial solutions but no definitive ones. Several different adaptive filter algorithms can be made to acquire and track the sinusoidal signal and so improve the signal-to-noise ratio. One particular type of filter is the adaptive line enhancer (ALE), which is at its most efficient when executed with an IIR adaptive section. The principle of the basic structure of the ALE is explained and experimental procedures discussed. The adjustment of pole frequency and radius are described, with consideration of the normalised least mean squares (NLMS) algorithm.

articleTitle: An integrated approach to the design and implementation of image filters
publicationTitle: IEE 15th SARAGA Colloquium on Digital and Analogue Filters and Filtering Systems
abstract: This paper presents a flexible and integrated design methodology for image filtering hardware that allows the development of high level algorithms and the automation of their ASIC implementation. The proposed approach offers the algorithm developer all the necessary tools to design and simulate the image processing algorithms at a high level of abstraction, and without any hardware constraints. Once the algorithm has been completely specified its high level description is synthesised, with minimum intervention from the algorithm developer, to one of several levels of hardware description including RTL VHDL and a netlist of the ASIC target technology. The proposed development process uses Mentor Graphics DSP Station. DSP Station is a development system for signal processing hardware and it is not offered as an image processing development tool. This paper describes the adaptation of DSP Station as an integrated environment for the development of image processing algorithms and their ASIC implementation. The design methodology is illustrated by an example algorithm of a 2-D image filter and its architectural implementation.

articleTitle: A performance assessment of audio filters using current-mode analogue devices
publicationTitle: IEE 15th SARAGA Colloquium on Digital and Analogue Filters and Filtering Systems
abstract: The practical performances of second-order active filters using voltage operational amplifiers, current conveyors and transconductance amplifiers are compared. Integrated-circuit current-conveyor realizations have some significant advantages apart from impaired noise level.

articleTitle: Current practices and future directions for adaptive digital filters in telecommunications applications
publicationTitle: IEE 15th SARAGA Colloquium on Digital and Analogue Filters and Filtering Systems
abstract: This paper considers two research areas in adaptive digital filtering where efforts are being made to improve the state of the art for high speed adaptive processing of images and image sequences, as might be encountered in digital video systems. The first area concerns the development of two dimensional (2D) adaptive digital filtering concepts for use in digital video systems, while the second concerns the guaranteeing of reliable adaptive processing through the concept of adaptive fault tolerance.

articleTitle: How not to design an active filter-thoughts on the choice of op-amps
publicationTitle: IEE 15th SARAGA Colloquium on Digital and Analogue Filters and Filtering Systems
abstract: Considers some of the issues which are too often forgotten when active filters are being designed. As a practising applications engineer working for an op-amp manufacturer the author is accustomed to being blamed for the failure of active filter designs to meet their specifications and would like to share a few insights on the choice of opamps.

articleTitle: From specification to implementation-the application of high-performance tools to the design of a digital filter for DECT
publicationTitle: IEE 15th SARAGA Colloquium on Digital and Analogue Filters and Filtering Systems
abstract: In this paper a case-study is presented describing the design of a digital recursive filter using DSP Station from Mentor Graphics. The designed filter is part of an ADPCM Transcoder IC for the DECT (Digital European Cordless Telephone) standard. This IC includes on-board sigma-delta AD/DA converters. The paper shows the design of the digital filter starting from a frequency domain specification using tools for filter synthesis, frequency domain simulation, coefficient optimisation, finite wordlength effect analysis and high-level synthesis. A comparison between a standard biquad structure and a wave digital filter (WDF) structure is made. The resulting bitserial RTL level netlist generated by the high-level synthesis tool, Mistral, can be used for FPGA, standard cell or gate array implementation.

articleTitle: Analysis of digital IIR filters with maximum usable bandwidth for phased array radars
publicationTitle: IEE 15th SARAGA Colloquium on Digital and Analogue Filters and Filtering Systems
abstract: This paper deals with the analysis of digital IIR filters with maximum usable bandwidth. These filters are useful for rejecting narrow band clutter in radar applications. Zero frequency initialisation is used as a pre-design technique to achieve good clutter rejection capability while operating in the transient. The analysis covered the variation in the cut-off frequency of the filter caused by changing the number of samples. The effect of processing a number of samples other than the one the filter is designed for is also, covered. First and second order filters with numbers of samples up to 20 are investigated.

articleTitle: A filter compiler under pressure: unusual approximations and realisations
publicationTitle: IEE 15th SARAGA Colloquium on Digital and Analogue Filters and Filtering Systems
abstract: The demands upon filter compilers continue to increase. Mixed-mode signal processing systems extend over an enormous frequency range and generate filter specifications which range from the sublime to the ridiculous (almost). Some specifications can be met by traditional approximation and filter realisation; others need the application of very powerful approximators and efficient circuit realisations to produce solutions that are viable as integrated circuits without impossible demands for chip area and power consumption or degradation in circuit performance due to accuracy problems or noise behaviour. The XFILT software provides a comprehensive active filter compiler which is finding application in areas where signal filtering and delay equalisation is required. It has been used in the real design world over a wide range of frequencies and it is hoped that further extensions will enlarge the field of application.

articleTitle: Current mode filters: design, simulation and implementation
publicationTitle: IEE 15th SARAGA Colloquium on Digital and Analogue Filters and Filtering Systems
abstract: This paper describes the design, simulation and implementation of a number of current-mode based filters. Three current devices are considered: current conveyors, transconductance and current feedback amplifiers. Simulation and measured results of a 4/sup th/ order, 0.1 dB Chebyshev lowpass filter with a bandwidth of 5 MHz are included.

articleTitle: Quadrature-mirror-filter design for the subband coding of digital video signals
publicationTitle: IEE 15th SARAGA Colloquium on Digital and Analogue Filters and Filtering Systems
abstract: The paper firstly reviews the basic two-channel subband coding system and its implementation using both quadrature mirror filter (QMF) and conjugate quadrature filter (CQF) designs. Their features and performance characteristics for the one-dimensional case are examined and then using the principle of separability, 2-D QMF-CQF implementations are constructed, as the product of two l-D transfer functions. Examples of 2-D QMF-CQFs in band-splitting configurations for video applications are explored and discussed.

articleTitle: All pass filter implementation using reflection coefficient of lossless networks
publicationTitle: IEE 15th SARAGA Colloquium on Digital and Analogue Filters and Filtering Systems
abstract: All pass filters are increasingly important as components in digital communications systems, and, although digital baseband realizations are increasingly important, passive analogue filters remain the lowest cost implementations and those with the lowest power consumption for many radio applications. Conventional approaches are based an two port networks with bridged T and lattice structures. These require accurate matching of components to maintain the all-pass characteristics. This paper describes theoretical work and the results of simulation and experiment on the implementation of all pass networks and the related problem of voltage controlled phase shifting networks (for such applications as diversity combining) based on the reflection coefficient of lossless networks.

articleTitle: Design of PCAS structures to meet arbitrary specifications using a phase design technique
publicationTitle: IEE 15th SARAGA Colloquium on Digital and Analogue Filters and Filtering Systems
abstract: The parallel combination of allpass subfilters (PCAS) is a highly efficient filter structure suitable for use in high performance filtering applications. The structure has been widely applied to the design of filters to meet stringent specifications in terms of magnitude and phase, or group delay. This paper presents a design method, for these types of specifications, that formulates the design purely in terms of the filter phase. This leads to an efficient, reliable design method. Comparison is made between this and previously published design methods.

articleTitle: Optimisation of complex recursive digital filters operating in transient mode
publicationTitle: IEE 15th SARAGA Colloquium on Digital and Analogue Filters and Filtering Systems
abstract: This paper describes a design method for recursive filters with complex coefficients and operating in the transient mode. The non-zero frequency initialisation technique is used as a pre-design method to force a notch at any frequency. The design method is based on a minimax approach to achieve the desired frequency response. Different filters were designed by the new method for rejecting clutter in radar applications.
